newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - April 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - April 24.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Fifteen prisoners have allegedly raped four Lao women in front of scores of other detainees in a cell at police station in Rayong province. According to police, the four women were arrested for gambling and illegal entry into Thailand. Police say no other prisoners dare to help the women for fear that the alleged rapists were influential. (THE NATION)

- Interior Minister Snoh Thienthong has moved to delay the arrest of New Aspiration Party MP Chatthawat Muttamara and seven others in connection with the 17th case in the Bangkok Bank of Commerce (BBC) loan scandal. Meanwhile, the acting chief of the Economic Crime Investigation Division has called on politicians and others involved in the scandal to return money to the BBC so that cases against them could be dropped. (THE NATON)

- Garlic growers have laid siege to Chiang Mai city hall and set up a road block in Mae Hong Son province to demand government action over the low price of their produce. They want the government to guarantee them a price of 17-20 baht per kilogramme of garlic - the current market price is five or six baht a kilo. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Royal Decree on the establishment of the Property Loan Management Organization (PLMO) has been signed by His Majesty the King, setting the stage for the Government's massive rescue effort of the property and financial sectors, says a source in the Bank of Thailand. The primary function of the PLMO will be to purchase collateralized property loans from financial institutions, thereby injecting liquidity into the financial sector as well as the property sector. (BUSINESS DAY)

- Thai Shipowners' Association has proposed the establishment of a National Shipping Line with at least 51 percent to be held by a group of Thai carriers. The proposal was made after the Transport and Communications Ministry's committee on the establishment of a national shipping line concluded a framework which it submitted to Transport Minister Suwat Liptapanlop for approval. (THE NATION)
